dossier.purpose: Python library from LangChain (pyproject.toml version 0.0.30) for adding long-term memory to LLM agents. It provides: LLM-driven extraction and consolidation of memories (a stateless "functional core" plus a store-backed manager); LangChain tools an agent can call to create, update, delete and search memories in a LangGraph BaseStore; a background "reflection" executor; prompt optimizers; and message-history summarization. It ships no storage engine, CLI, MCP server, daemon, or Claude Code/Codex integration. Persistence is whatever LangGraph BaseStore the host application supplies, and every extraction step calls an external LLM provider.

claims.claim: LangMem helps agents learn and adapt from their interactions over time; it provides tooling to extract important information from conversations, optimize agent behavior through prompt refinement, and maintain long-term memory.
It offers both functional primitives you can use with any storage system and native integration with LangGraph's storage layer.
Agents can continuously improve, personalize their responses, and maintain consistent behavior across sessions.
Key feature: 'Core memory API that works with any storage system'.
Key feature: 'Memory management tools that agents can use to record and search information during active conversations "in the hot path"'.
Key feature: 'Background memory manager that automatically extracts, consolidates, and updates agent knowledge'.
Key feature: 'Native integration with LangGraph's Long-term Memory Store, available by default in all LangGraph Platform deployments'.
Install with `pip install -U langmem`, then 'Configure your environment with an API key for your favorite LLM provider' (example: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
The memory tools work in any LangGraph app, and can be added to existing agents or used to build custom memory systems without agents.
InMemoryStore keeps memories in process memory and they are lost on restart; for production use AsyncPostgresStore or a similar DB-backed store to persist memories across server restarts.
The memory tools let you control what gets stored; the agent extracts key information, maintains memory consistency, and knows when to search past interactions.
The agent decides what and when to store a memory; no special commands needed, the agent uses create_manage_memory_tool.
The LLM can invoke create_search_memory_tool to search for memories with similar content; the hot path quickstart shows how to include memories without the agent explicitly searching.

Required or likely network services: (1) An LLM provider API for every extraction, consolidation, query-generation, summarization and prompt-optimization step, via init_chat_model (src/langmem/knowledge/extraction.py:229, 779, 853); conversation text is embedded in the prompts (extraction.py:457-478). An API key is required (README.md:24-28), and langchain-openai and langchain-anthropic are both hard dependencies (pyproject.toml:11,14). (2) An embeddings provider for semantic search when the store is indexed; the README example uses `openai:text-embedding-3-small` (README.md:41-45), and the standalone README says to set OPENAI_API_KEY (examples/standalone_examples/README.md:27-31). (3) A persistent store backend (e.g. Postgres via LangGraph) for durability; langmem ships none (README.md:62). (4) Optional LangGraph server for RemoteReflectionExecutor (src/langmem/reflection.py:157-198; docs/docs/guides/delayed_processing.md:75-84). (5) Optional LangSmith: prompt-optimizer code wraps calls in langsmith `trace` spans (src/langmem/prompts/optimization.py:295,381; gradient.py:331,371; metaprompt.py:98,124; stateless.py:66,97,193,225). Whether spans are exported depends on LangSmith/LangChain environment settings outside this repo, which I did not verify. The repo's deployment auth module (src/langmem/graphs/auth.py:20-45, wired at langgraph.json:8-10) requires an X-Api-Key header validated against LangSmith's /auth/public endpoint. Docs build only: Google Analytics, a GitHub API key secret for git-committers (.github/workflows/deploy_docs.yml:63-64), and fetching docs.python.org objects.inv (docs/mkdocs.yml:65).

code.architecture: Pure-Python library (about 6.9k lines in src/langmem, much of it docstrings), layered on LangChain/LangGraph; there is no storage engine, server or local file I/O. src/langmem/knowledge/extraction.py: MemoryManager builds a `trustcall.create_extractor` call with Pydantic schemas and instructions, and returns inserts, updates and RemoveDoc items (deletes are off by default). MemoryStoreManager wraps it: it searches the BaseStore for up to query_limit (default 5) relevant memories, calls the manager, then writes `{kind, content}` values with store.aput and hard-deletes with store.adelete. Optional `phases` run extra consolidation passes. src/langmem/knowledge/tools.py provides the LLM-callable manage_memory and search_memory tools, taking the store from `store=` or the LangGraph context. src/langmem/utils.py: NamespaceTemplate resolves `{var}` namespace segments from RunnableConfig['configurable']. src/langmem/reflection.py is the background executor. src/langmem/prompts/ holds the gradient, metaprompt and prompt_memory optimizers (optimization.py, gradient.py, metaprompt.py, stateless.py); _layers.py is marked non-public and stateful.py is not imported anywhere. src/langmem/short_term/summarization.py provides message summarization. src/langmem/graphs/ holds the LangGraph-server graphs plus the LangSmith-header auth. src/langmem/graph_rag.py is entirely commented out. Persistence, vector indexing, TTL and history are delegated to whichever langgraph BaseStore the host supplies; langmem itself stores only `{kind, content}` (store manager, extraction.py:1114,1122) or `{content}` (tools, tools.py:301), with no provenance, author or version fields.
code.packaging_and_release: Build backend is hatchling (pyproject.toml:22-24); wheel/sdist exclude tests, docs, evals and notebooks (pyproject.toml:76-92); version 0.0.30 (pyproject.toml:3). The only release workflow is .github/workflows/release.yml. It is manual (`workflow_dispatch`, line 7), runs on ubuntu-latest, pins uv 0.6.3 (lines 17-22), then `uv build` and `uv publish` with a long-lived `secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN` (lines 30-36). Workflow permissions are `contents: read` only (lines 3-4), with no `id-token`, so there is no trusted-publishing or attestation step. I found no checksum, signature, SBOM or GitHub-release step, no test gate before publish, and no tag trigger. Actions are pinned by tag, not SHA (checkout@v4, setup-uv@v5, setup-python@v5). The checkout is shallow, so I could not list upstream tags.

claim_checks.claim: Core memory API that works with any storage system (README.md:13)
claim_checks.evidence: create_memory_manager returns MemoryManager (src/langmem/knowledge/extraction.py:217-534, 536-692), which takes an optional `existing` list and returns ExtractedMemory items with no store reference. docs/docs/guides/extract_semantic_memories.md:85 says it does not read or write a database. Caveats: the package hard-depends on langgraph and both LLM provider packages (pyproject.toml:8-17), and an LLM call is always required.

claim_checks.claim: Memory tools let agents record and search information during active conversations (README.md:14)
claim_checks.evidence: create_manage_memory_tool (src/langmem/knowledge/tools.py:25-356) supports create/update/delete by UUID key, writing `{content: ...}` (tools.py:297-303). create_search_memory_tool (tools.py:362-486) calls store.search. Both need a BaseStore, either `store=` or the LangGraph context (tools.py:489-497); otherwise they raise ConfigurationError.

claim_checks.claim: Background memory manager that automatically extracts, consolidates, and updates agent knowledge (README.md:15)
claim_checks.evidence: MemoryStoreManager.ainvoke/invoke (extraction.py:1006-1137, 1139-1280) does search, LLM and put/delete, but only when the host application calls it or calls ReflectionExecutor.submit; nothing schedules itself. The local executor is an in-process non-daemon thread with an in-memory PriorityQueue (reflection.py:264-270), so pending work is not persisted and the process will not exit until shutdown() is called (reflection.py:369-379). The remote executor creates LangGraph server runs (reflection.py:182-195). Consolidation only sees the top query_limit (default 5) retrieved memories (extraction.py:847, 1039).

claim_checks.claim: Native integration with LangGraph's Long-term Memory Store, available by default in all LangGraph Platform deployments (README.md:16)
claim_checks.evidence: BaseStore integration is confirmed (tools.py:7-8, 489-497; extraction.py:12-16, 897-913; langgraph.json:11-17). 'Available by default in all LangGraph Platform deployments' depends on the platform and cannot be checked from this repo; docs/docs/hot_path_quickstart.md:111 says a Postgres-backed store is provided automatically.

claim_checks.claim: InMemoryStore loses memories on restart; use AsyncPostgresStore or a similar DB-backed store for persistence (README.md:62)
claim_checks.evidence: Store implementations live in langgraph, which is not vendored here. In-repo facts: langmem contains no persistence code (no open()/sqlite/pathlib in src/). Every runnable sample constructs InMemoryStore (32 occurrences across 16 files) and there is no PostgresStore/from_conn_string usage anywhere (grep returns 0). examples/standalone_examples/README.md:13 lists a 'Persistent Store Example' as 'Coming Soon'.

claim_checks.claim: Quickstart needs only an LLM provider API key (README.md:24-28)
claim_checks.evidence: The README snippet also builds an index with `embed: openai:text-embedding-3-small` (README.md:41-45), which needs OpenAI credentials, but only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is shown. examples/standalone_examples/README.md:27-31 does say to set OPENAI_API_KEY. The README uses the model alias `anthropic:claude-3-5-sonnet-latest` (README.md:50); whether that alias is still served was not checked.

claim_checks.claim: The agent 'knows when to search past interactions' (README.md:64)
claim_checks.evidence: The mechanism is plain LLM tool-calling. The search tool's default instructions are empty (`_MEMORY_SEARCH_INSTRUCTIONS = ""`, tools.py:359), so its description is one generic sentence (tools.py:476-478), while the manage tool carries explicit when-to-call guidance (tools.py:28-32). Behaviour depends on the model; the repo contains no evals (`evals/` is git-ignored, .gitignore:175; pyproject.toml:56).

claim_checks.claim: create_memory_store_manager 'maintains a versioned history of all changes' (docstring, src/langmem/knowledge/extraction.py:1684-1685)
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from the docstring. The store manager writes with store.aput to the same namespace/key (extraction.py:1107-1124, 1132-1133) and hard-deletes with store.adelete (extraction.py:1126-1135, 1274-1278); the manage tool overwrites on update and hard-deletes on delete (tools.py:293-303). A grep of src/ for version/history/tombstone/restore/audit/undo finds only this docstring line. Any history would have to come from the BaseStore backend, not from this repo.

The factory default is False (extraction.py:1675). The MemoryStoreManager class default is True (extraction.py:845). Entries in `phases` default to enable_deletes=True (extraction.py:988), so phase managers can emit deletes even when the top-level flag is False. Deletes are applied as hard store.adelete / store.delete (extraction.py:1134, 1278). The manage_memory tool permits delete by default (tools.py:34-36).

claim_checks.claim: 'You can also process memories directly with `memory_manager.process(messages)`' (docs/docs/background_quickstart.md:82, linked from README.md:96)
claim_checks.evidence: No `process` method exists in src/ (grep for `def process` finds nothing; the only occurrence is that docs line). Direct calls use invoke / ainvoke / __call__ (extraction.py:1006, 1139, 1282).

risks: Scope: this is a library, not a memory service. No CLI, MCP server, daemon, hook, or Claude Code/Codex integration exists (pyproject.toml has no scripts; grep for MCP/codex/claude-code finds nothing). Sharing one memory between two separate agent CLIs would need a host application or bridge that someone else writes. Durability and cross-process sharing depend entirely on an external LangGraph BaseStore, and every sample in the repo uses InMemoryStore (README.md:62; examples/standalone_examples/README.md:13).

Recovery and audit: updates overwrite the same key and deletes are hard deletes with no tombstone, undo or history (tools.py:293-303; extraction.py:1118-1135). The docstring promising a 'versioned history' (extraction.py:1684-1685) has no implementation. Stored values carry only {kind, content} or {content}, with no provenance, author, source-message or version fields (extraction.py:1114,1122; tools.py:301). No backup, export or audit feature is documented.

Delete controls are inconsistent and LLM-driven: manage_memory allows delete by default (tools.py:34-36); create_memory_store_manager defaults enable_deletes=False (extraction.py:1675) while its docstring says True (1706-1707), the class default is True (845), and `phases` default to True (988). The Local ReflectionExecutor queue is in memory and its worker is a non-daemon thread, so a short-lived process that never calls shutdown() will not exit (reflection.py:264-270, 369-379).

Every capture decision is an LLM prompt (extraction.py:185-206, 457-478), so results are non-deterministic and conversation text goes to the configured LLM provider. Semantic search needs an embeddings provider (README.md:41-45); the shipped langgraph.json and examples are wired to OpenAI/Anthropic, and a LangSmith key is required for the repo's deployment auth (graphs/auth.py:20-45). No benchmarks or evals are published, and `evals/` is git-ignored (.gitignore:175).

Test and CI coverage: no CI workflow runs pytest or ruff on src/ (only deploy_docs.yml and release.yml). The suite is 30 offline summarization tests plus a parametrized docstring runner that needs live API keys and a `langgraph dev` server (tests/test_docstring_examples.py:235-297; Makefile:17-25). There are no unit tests for tools.py, MemoryStoreManager, reflection.py or utils.py.

Compatibility: pyproject.toml:6 declares Python >=3.10, but extraction.py:69 evaluates `typing.NotRequired` (Python 3.11+) in a class body without `from __future__ import annotations`, and graphs/auth.py:2 imports it. By static reading, `import langmem` would fail on 3.10 (not executed here). The repo only exercises Python 3.11 and 3.12 (Makefile:19; deploy_docs.yml:43). langmem imports langgraph internals (`langgraph._internal._constants`, reflection.py:14; `langgraph.utils.config`, utils.py:9) against a wide range `langgraph>=0.6.0,<2` (pyproject.toml:13). The project is pre-1.0 (0.0.30), and _layers.py:1 says it is not public API and may change.

Release and supply chain: publishing is a manual workflow using a long-lived PyPI API token (release.yml:7,33-36), with no attestations, checksums or signatures, no tests before publish, and actions pinned by tag rather than SHA (release.yml:15,18,25; deploy_docs.yml:29). No SECURITY.md exists, so there is no documented vulnerability-reporting path. LICENSE is MIT (copyright 2025 LangChain); licenses of the 163 locked transitive packages were not audited.

Docs and code drift, plus dead code: docs reference a nonexistent `memory_manager.process` (background_quickstart.md:82) and missing scripts plus poetry (docs/README.md:5-6, 22-23). pyproject.toml:55-56 lists a workspace member that is not in the checkout. graph_rag.py is fully commented out. prompts/stateful.py is unused and hard-codes `claude-3-5-sonnet-latest` (stateful.py:17-19). _layers.py:139-142 calls create_memory_searcher with arguments its signature (extraction.py:695-700) does not accept. Examples pin Anthropic aliases such as `claude-3-5-sonnet-latest` (README.md:50), whose availability was not verified.

checks.note: The verdict 'no' and every code citation are correct. The docstring text is at extraction.py:1684-1685. Updates aput to the existing old_art.namespace/old_art.key (1107-1116, 1132-1133).
